narrative:
Our risk assessment estimates an 82% probability that you would default on the loan. Out of every 100 applicants with a similar financial profile, roughly 82 are expected to become delinquent, making this loan too risky to approve.

The primary factor behind this decision is your checking account, which is currently overdrawn—a situation seen in only about one in eight approved applicants. Most approved borrowers keep a positive balance or have no checking account at all. This alone pushes strongly toward denial, as it signals your day-to-day finances are already under stress.

The second most influential factor is the length of credit you requested: 48 months, more than double the typical 19 months among approved borrowers. While a longer term lowers monthly payments, it also extends the window of risk, giving more time for your financial situation to change for the worse. This too pushed the decision against you.

Third, your savings buffer is very thin. With less than 100 Deutsche Marks set aside, you have little fallback if an unexpected expense or loss of income occurs, whereas most approved applicants demonstrate a stronger cushion.

To improve your chances, rebuild your savings to cover several months of essentials, keep your checking account out of overdraft, and request a smaller loan with a shorter term that matches your current income. Sustained responsible account management over the coming year will show lenders you are a safer risk.
